new_statements.quote: 在苗語中，川黔滇方言貴陽次方言、惠水次方言、重安江次方言和湘西方言都沒有入聲調，川黔滇方言滇東北次方言、平塘次方言只有一個入聲調，川黔滇次方言和黔東方言基本上保留著入聲調，但也不是絕對的。沒有入聲調並不等於入聲調消失了，只是入聲調合併到別的調類中去了。貴陽次方言的擺托、惠水次方言的高坡都是 D1 調並入 C1 調，D2 調並入 A2調 (p.701) ... 苗語湘西方言西部土語如臘乙坪、貴陽次方言如擺托、惠水次方言如甲定、重安江次方言如楓香都是六聲六類 (p.705)
new_statements.translation: Within Miao, the Guiyang, Huishui and Chong'anjiang subdialects of the Chuanqiandian dialect and the Xiangxi dialect all have no entering (D) tones; the Diandongbei and Pingtang subdialects have only one entering tone; the Chuanqiandian subdialect and the Qiandong dialect basically keep the entering tones, though not absolutely. Having no entering tone does not mean the entering tone vanished; it merged into other tone categories. In Baituo (Guiyang subdialect) and Gaopo (Huishui subdialect) tone D1 merged into C1 and D2 into A2 (p.701) ... Layiping (W. Xiangxi), Baituo (Guiyang subdialect), Jiading (Huishui subdialect) and Fengxiang (Chong'anjiang) are all 'six tones, six categories' (p.705).

The claim is made for the Huishui subdialect (惠水次方言) as a whole and exemplified only by Gaopo/Jiading, the Northern Huishui point (nort2749); the paper's 31-variety list has no Eastern Huishui datapoint. Tonal status is not in doubt, but the statement is subdialect-level, not about east2372. | checker: Re-downloaded https://www.ling.sinica.edu.tw/item/en?act=journal&code=download&article_id=104 (HTTP 200, PDF 1.6, 30 pp); In the extracted text file the p.701-702 passage (the text layer: '在苗語中，川黔滇方言貴陽次方言、惠水次方言、重安江次方言和湘西方言都沒有入聲調.. 貴陽次方言的擺托、惠水次方言的高坡都是 D1 調並入 C1 調，D2 調並入 A2 調') and the p.705 passage (lines 1016-1017: '惠水次方言如甲定.. 都是六聲六類') match A's quote c…

new_statements.rule_in_words: Lexical tone language: the Huishui subdialect (to which Eastern Huishui belongs) lacks separate entering-tone categories (proto D tones merged into other categories; at the Northern Huishui point D1>C1, D2>A2, giving six tones). Nothing is said about word stress/accent.
new_statements.exceptions: none for Huishui; author notes tone mergers differ by language/dialect and that Chuanqiandian/Qiandong retention of D tones 'is not absolute'
new_statements.identity_note: Family-wide tone paper by the fieldworker who classified the southern-Guizhou Hmongic lects (Li 2000). Its statements about 惠水次方言 (the Huishui subdialect, which by Wang 1985/Li 2000 comprises the Northern hmi, Central hmc, Southwestern hmh and Eastern hme vernaculars) are exemplified only with the NORTHERN point 甲定/高坡 (Jiading, Gaopo = nort2749); there is no Xiguan/Baibang (hme) data point among the 31 varieties listed on pp.683-685. So the claim covers hme only as a member of the subdialect. Not in east2372's bibliography (a copy was read earlier for chua1256 and judged silent on Huishui prosody/stress). | Family-wide article (the source behind Ratliff 2010's 'prefixes are unstressed'); already on our list as 'paywalled DOI, unread'. New: the NCPSSD abstract was read and the full text is obtainable with a free NCPSSD account (access should read 'login (free registration)', not publisher paywall). No Eastern Huishui point is expected among its data.

new_statements.quote: 苗瑶语几乎没有构形词缀,构词词缀以前缀为多。前缀的语音特点是轻读;声母一般是塞音;韵母是单元音,往往与词根和谐;各方言都同源。... 前缀随着语音的演变,特别是阴阳调的分化而趋于消失
new_statements.translation: Hmong-Mien has almost no inflectional affixes; derivational affixes are mostly prefixes. Phonetically the prefixes are read lightly (unstressed); their initial is usually a stop; their final is a single vowel that often harmonises with the root; they are cognate across dialects. ... With sound change, especially the yin/yang tone split, prefixes tend to disappear.
new_statements.citation: 陈其光 Chen Qiguang. 1993. 苗瑶语前缀 [Prefixes in Miao-Yao]. 民族语文 Minzu Yuwen 1993(1): 1-9.
new_statements.locator: NCPSSD record 1003332231, remark (author abstract); article pp.1-9
new_statements.check: not checked by the second reader
new_statements.relation_note: Prefixes are unstressed/lightly read, monophthongal, harmonising with the root, and erode with tonal splits - family-level; tone otherwise presupposed.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Family-level: in prefix + root words the prefix is weak/unstressed (轻读) and the root carries full tone and prominence; no language-specific placement rule and no Eastern Huishui data seen.
new_statements.exceptions: abstract: prefix inventory is uneven across dialects ('除苗语西部方言个别点外..')
